## Shared ground — CJ0 and shared infrastructure

This is the part of road map "creator-jobs" (`designs/creator-jobs.md`) that no single bet owns:
the scope and the record (CJ0a), the tolls (CJ0b, CJ0c, CJ0d), the key rule (CJ1), and the
infrastructure two or more bets would otherwise build twice or collide on (CJ2a, CJ2b, CJ3, CJ4,
CJ6). The six bets (TX transcript, CU cursor and recorder, VR vertical, FC find clips, SW switch
by speaker, CO cutout and layouts) are designed elsewhere. This section names what they build on,
reconciles what their sections assumed about it ("What the bets build on"), and sets the order
they run in. Line counts are `wc -l` at `d0661e5d` (main, 2026-11-01).

### Goal

A person gets two things from the shared phases directly, and everything else through the bets:

- **Honest AI controls.** A command that would send to Claude or AssemblyAI is greyed out when its
  key is missing, and its tooltip says which key and where to set it. An agent's call that would
  send is refused with the same sentence. Nothing falls back to a weaker on-device model. Results
  already paid for keep working without a key.
- **Split at Shot Changes.** Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes cuts a flattened video (a finished edit,
  a downloaded clip, a stream VOD) at each hard cut, as one undo step. It is the first command on
  the analysis lane and the lane's proof in real use.

For the bets, the shared phases provide: one gate for keys; one lane, one store, one reader and
one sheet for every analysis of pictures and sounds, with hard cuts and face samples as its first
kinds; source ranges on the three placement ops; a decided clip ceiling; the files at the cap cut
once, before three lanes reach for them; and the record (decisions, IDs, lanes, trial, samples).
A new project from a range of the timeline is FC1 and FC2's (bet 4), not a shared phase: only FC
uses it.

### Owner's answers applied

The owner's answers of 2026-11-01, verbatim: "Add all: 1-6. Remove all explicit non-goals. The
recorder can ask for input monitoring. Anything that requires significant AI should require that
the user has supplied a key. Otherwise disable. 'Cutting one real video per lead segment in Frame
Job alongside the first bet' OK. Create a full design, then we'll compact and begin."

The orchestrator's reading, which the owner can change:

- **"Add all: 1-6"** is all six bets of `designs/creator-survey.md` "The bets" (lines 173–356),
  in one road map. The survey's next tier (lines 358–369) and its "Not worth chasing" table
  (lines 371–391) are not in it, and are neither in nor out.
- **"Remove all explicit non-goals"** answers survey decision 2 ("Which spec §1 non-goals to lift,
  and how far", line 396). It lifts every exclusion spec §1's non-goal paragraph names
  (`designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md:13–40`), read the same way throughout: the five non-goals
  themselves; the clauses later decisions added to that paragraph ("nothing else is scriptable",
  G-1; "hosting third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out", AU-2; "callouts reconstructed after
  the fact stay out", `recording.md` and CAM-1); and the grading features the paragraph quotes as
  "not wanted" (GR-20, GR-27…GR-30). It also lifts the bar sentence's "without … multicam, scopes,
  or a plugin ecosystem" (`:9–11`) and §2's "Left out" list (`designs/spec/02-six-ideas.md:24–26`),
  which is the same kind of statement. Lifting makes an item allowed, not scheduled. Decisions that
  shape what is built, rather than exclude something, stand until a phase amends one in writing:
  G-1's "a graphic is a source", R5-1's closed vocabularies, and "a recording is ordinary media"
  (CJ-1). CJ0a asks the owner to confirm the literal reading of the "not wanted" verdicts.
- **"The recorder can ask for input monitoring"** answers survey decision 4: the recorder panel
  may ask for the Input Monitoring grant, opt-in, for CU's shortcut capture (CJ-4).
- **"Anything that requires significant AI should require … a key. Otherwise disable."** answers
  survey decisions 6 and 7: Claude only on the person's Anthropic key, no Apple FoundationModels
  fallback, and filler detection stays AssemblyAI's (TR-7 stands). It applies to the shipped
  features as well as the new ones (CJ-3). On-device Apple frameworks and the models already
  bundled are not "significant AI".
- **The trial** answers survey decision 9: the owner cuts one talking-head video and one screen
  tutorial in Frame Job alongside TX, against criteria fixed before TX1's code. It is recorded in
  the road map's "Trial" section and under CJ-5, as grading's trial was under GR-1 and GR-9; it is
  not a standing check (CJ-5).
- **Not answered, asked at the phase that needs it:** survey decision 5 (a vertical copy or
  linked versions; VR7), 8 (the multi-stream 4K and multi-hour measurement; SW-S2, recommended as
  SW's first spike), 10 (positioning; not a build question).

### How it fits the tree

**Where the non-goals are stated.** Only in the spec and in §11 entries that cite it:

- `designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md` (47 lines): "Mac only" at 7; the bar sentence at 9–11; the
  non-goal paragraph at 13–40 (multicam; grading beyond per-clip controls with its GR
  parentheticals, among them "not wanted" GR-20 and GR-27…GR-30; a plugin system with G-1's
  clause; motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe, "heavy pixel work or
  ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape — road map 2 §4"; any platform but macOS; and the
  reversals for screen recording, camera recording and audio, with their "stays out" clauses).
- `designs/spec/02-six-ideas.md` (26 lines): "Left out: … callouts, pointer effects), templates,
  publishing to YouTube/Vimeo, the stock-media library" at 24–26.
- `designs/spec/README.md:20`: the index row says §1 holds "its non-goals"; its Lines cells for
  01 and 02 are checked by `tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py` in `make test`.
- §11 entries that state or rely on the list: `recording.md:6–15` (callouts stay OUT, "nothing
  is reconstructed afterwards"), `camera-recording.md:15–38` (CAM-1, callouts stay OUT),
  `graphics.md:6–16` (G-1 and its clause), `audio.md:52–59` (AU-2's "Out, under §1's plugin
  system"), `grading.md:26–36` (GR-1, amends §1), `effects-motion.md:6–10` (R5-1), and the "not
  wanted" verdicts (GR-20 in `grading-3.md:466`, GR-27…GR-30 in `grading-4.md:99–108`).
- Not stated anywhere else: `README.md`, `docs/guide/` and the three `CLAUDE.md` files hold no
  non-goal (grep for multicam, plugin, reframe, stabilis, motion blur, platform, callout).
  `CONTEXT.md:37,57` lists "plugin" as a word to avoid, which is vocabulary and stays.
  `designs/adr/` is history and is not edited.

**Keys today.** Two keys, two stores, seven separate "is there a key" reads, three behaviours.

- `SecretStore.swift` (235): the `SecretStore` protocol, a `0600` `FileStore` and a
  `MemoryStore`. AssemblyAI's file is `assemblyai-key`, the Assistant's `anthropic-key`, both
  in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/` (R6-5, AI-8).
- `AssemblyAIConfiguration.swift` (179): `store()` at 135 (R6-9: `-RCSecretFolder`, or an empty
  `MemoryStore` under `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint`), `credential(store:environment:)` at 150 (the
  file, then `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY`). `AssistantConfiguration.swift` (216): `store()` at 78 (AI-13:
  `-RCSecretFolder`, or empty under `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL`), `credential` at 97 (the file, then
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), `didChangeNotification` at 138. `SettingsWindowController.swift` (463)
  posts its own `didChangeNotification` after Save (`:391`), Remove (`:405`) and a region change
  (`:416`).
- The sheets take their store and environment as injected values with today's defaults:
  `FillerSheetController.swift:37`, `:98` and `TranscribeSheetController.swift:91`, `:170`. Probes
  build them over their own `MemoryStore` (`tools/proof/filler_sheet_probe.swift`,
  `word_captions_sheet_support.swift`, `sheet_chrome_probe.swift`).
- The reads that decide "a key is present", each its own: `FillerSheetController+Transcribe.swift:85`,
  `TranscribeSheetController+Cloud.swift:221` and `:250`, `EditorViewController+Assistant.swift:169–171`;
  and the sending sites `FillerSheetController+Transcribe.swift:144`,
  `TranscribeSheetController+Cloud.swift:292`, `AgentServer+Fillers.swift:143`,
  `AgentServer+CloudCaptions.swift:119`, `AssistantSession.swift:107`.
  `AssistantSettingsPane.swift:217` is not a gate: it words Settings' status line from the typed
  field and `MemoryStore(stored)`.
- **Remove Filler Words without a key:** the menu item is enabled whenever a clip plays sound from
  a media file (`FillerSheetController.swift:301–305`, `validateFillerAction` →
  `Transcriber.hasTranscribableClip`). The sheet opens and counts fillers from cached AssemblyAI
  transcripts; each media with no filler transcript gets a row whose Transcribe button is
  disabled with the note "No AssemblyAI API key is set — Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  (`FillerSheetController+Transcribe.swift:84–112`, `TranscribeSheetController+Cloud.swift:31`).
- **`transcribe_for_fillers` is keyed only when it would send.** Its order
  (`AgentServer+Fillers.swift:77–84`): the media id, a document with nowhere to keep the cache, a
  media no clip plays from its file, then the credential; a media that already has a filler
  transcript answers `ready: true` with no request and no key read, between the last two
  (`:125–135`). Only then is the credential read (`:143–147`), refusing with
  `CloudTranscriber.AccessError.credentialRequired` ("No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in
  Frame Job ▸ Settings ▸ Transcription, or RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY for a proof.",
  `CloudTranscriber.swift:56–62`). `detect_fillers` reads caches only and needs no key.
- **Generate Captions without a key:** the Engine popup always offers AssemblyAI, and its
  cloud-only options show only when it is chosen. `refreshCloud` computes
  `canReuseWithoutCredential` from those options (`TranscribeSheetController+Cloud.swift:216–241`);
  Start is enabled without a key only when every row can be served from a current transcript
  (R6-16), and the note reads the no-key sentence (`:238–240`, `:250–253`). `transcribe` with the
  cloud engine refuses in R6-17's precedence unless R6-16 admits the batch.
- **The Assistant without a key:** the composer is replaced by "Add your Anthropic API key in
  Settings to use the assistant." and a Settings button (`AssistantView.swift:25`, `:247–250`);
  a session refuses to open with a sentence citing AI-8 (`AssistantSession.swift:107–111`).
  View ▸ Assistant (⌃⌘A, `AppDelegate+Menus.swift:464`) is always enabled.
- AI-1 (`assistant.md:10`): the app never calls Anthropic itself; the bundled helper (`agent/`)
  does. `agent/src/` is byte-identical to Rasterize's but for three lines (root `CLAUDE.md`), so
  any new helper command is a change offered to both apps.

**Caches and analysis today.** No video analysis exists; `app/Sources` imports no Vision.

- `MediaCacheLane.swift` (78): the import pass's lane, width 2 (`:26–30`), audio decodes only
  (peaks, sync features, speech), never the cooperative pool (#367). Thumbnails are not on it.
- `MediaCacheLedger.swift` (231): one current pass per (package, media), generations (a changed
  Camera Log input starts a new one, `:52–58`, `:103–107`), and `CacheLedger.publish(in:for:_:)`
  (`:171`), which never writes while a save of the package is in flight and takes a nil pass.
- `MediaCacheFiles.swift` (452): `CacheStamp` (`:172–197`: size, modified second, duration,
  width, height, has video, has audio, and three import constants) and `SpeechStamp`
  (`:249–262`), which wraps it with the model, the chunk and a version — the shape a new stamp
  copies.
- `DeviceTranscriptCache.swift` (209): the on-demand per-media cache (TR-14): runs over source
  spans in media source ticks, a hit is a stored run containing the asked span, the OS version in
  the stamp. A transcript depends on its run's context, which is why TR-14 needs whole runs; an
  analysis kind whose values depend on one frame does not (CJ-22).
- `RampAudioRenders.swift`: the process-wide render queue for offline jobs (ramp, isolation,
  voice): owners want results, an unwanted job is cancelled, the export waits, and
  `-RCDevRampRenderHold <s>` (`:34`, `:273`) holds each render for a proof. The shape the analysis
  lane copies.
- `MediaImporter+ThumbnailSource.swift` (349): a strip of a log, HLG or PQ media is drawn through
  a one-clip composition and step 0. Its reader is an `AVAssetImageGenerator` (`ThumbnailReader`,
  `:159–189`) with ±0.5 s tolerance and the strip's `maximumSize` (`configure`, `:298–307`), so it
  cannot read every frame. The composition comes from `oneClip` (`:311`, `private`). The converted
  marker `ConvertedThumbsStamp` (`:114–157`) records what converted the picture: curve and gamut,
  or the LUT's path, size and second, or the HDR transfer, plus `fullRange` and a PQ peak.
- Every frame of a composition is read today by `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput`
  (`ExporterWriter+Settings.swift:41`, `DeepStillFrame.swift:68`).
- `BackgroundRender.swift`: knows every transport that has moved (`transports`, `:71`, `private`),
  so "is anything playing" is one accessor away.
- The E9 Vision spike (`tools/proof/effects_spike/vision_*.swift`, recorded in
  `designs/adr/effects-survey.md:264–285, 329–334`): person masks at `.balanced` run 4.2–5.5×
  realtime at 10 masks a second; results are byte-identical on one device, but GPU and Neural
  Engine differ by up to 25 levels; foreground masks flicker on video. Its fixtures read only art
  shipped with the system (`vision_fixtures.sh`: `/System/Library/Photos/Resources/FlexAudio/`'s
  album covers, frontal faces, one of two people). Its proposed D5 ("Vision, no shipped model,
  masks cached per media under stamp, marker and ledger") never entered §11.

**Placement today.**

**CJ0a's block (CJ0a, CJ0b, CJ0c and CJ0d share it).**

- **CJ-1 — Every exclusion spec §1 and §2 name is lifted; lifting one makes it allowed, not
  scheduled (owner, 2026-11-01: "Remove all explicit non-goals"; amends §1, §2, `recording.md`'s
  first bullet, CAM-1, AU-2, G-1, GR-20 and GR-27…GR-30).** Lifted: multicam; colour grading
  beyond per-clip controls (already in by GR-1 and its successors); a plugin system, and scripting
  beyond a graphic's module (G-1's clause); hosting third-party Audio Unit plug-ins (AU-2's out
  clause); motion blur; stabilisation; optical-flow retiming; auto-reframe; ML or heavy pixel work
  outside the compositor's one pass; callouts and reconstructing afterwards what the recorder saw

  a tooltip naming the key and where it is set, and every tool call that would send refuses in

**CJ2a's and CJ2b's block (the analysis lane).**

- **CJ-20 — Analysis is a cache, made on demand.** It never runs at import, is never project
  state, and is never read by the composition plan or the frame recipe. A planner reads it and
  writes ordinary edits. A render drawn from it (CO's masks) is substituted by Swift, as a
  reversed file is (§5.6). So no analysis kind bumps the format. VR-10's on-demand rule is this
  one; the speech cache's import-time rule stands for speech.
- **CJ-21 — One lane, `AnalysisLane`, process-wide, with two queues.** A picture queue (decodes
  and Vision) and a sound queue (audio decodes and Sound Analysis), so a sound job never waits
  behind a face job. Each is its own `DispatchQueue` at `.utility`, never the cooperative pool and
  never `MediaCacheLane`; the picture queue's width is spike CJ-S3's (1 until it earns 2), the
  sound queue's 1. A job is a source, a window and the kinds asked for it; kinds that share a
  reader, a size and a grid decode once (VR's subjects and CJ3's faces). Jobs are wanted by owners
  — a document's command, a tool call, an export — as ramp audio's renders are (SR-12): a job
  nobody wants is cancelled, one wanted again while it runs is not, `wait` returns on landing,
  failure or cancellation, and an owner's `settled` runs on main. A job takes no `CachePass` and
  writes only through `CacheLedger.publish(in:for: nil)`, so an import pass and an analysis job of
  the same media never cancel or wait on each other. `-RCDevAnalysisHold <s>` (a build with
  `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` only) holds each job for s seconds before its first frame, polling
  cancellation every 50 ms, as `-RCDevRampRenderHold` does. When CJ-S3's playback rule turns it
  on, the picture queue pauses between frames while any transport plays and resumes when none
  does, through a new internal `BackgroundRender.anyPlaying` over its `transports`
  (`BackgroundRender.swift:71`).
- **CJ-22 — The store.** A kind's results for one source are a marker,
  `cache/analysis/<kind>/<source>.json`, and a payload folder, `cache/analysis/<kind>/<source>/`,
  holding whatever files the kind names (`faces` a `samples.bin`, `shots` a `frames.bin`, CO's
  masks one movie per chunk). `<source>` is the media id, or `<media id>r` for a kind that reads a
  media's reversed render (CO-4). A kind whose variants must coexist puts the variant in its
  name (`masks-standard`, `masks-best`). Every kind has a grid on source time — frames by
  presentation time (`shots`), samples at k / rate (`faces`, `subjects`), fixed chunks (masks),
  windows at k × hop (`sound-events`) — and stores per grid point only values that depend on that
  point's input and a fixed neighbourhood the kind names (`shots`' two previous frames), never on
  where a job began or on what else is cached. Thresholds over time, minimum lengths, smoothing
  and identity are applied when a request is answered, over the requested window. The marker
  holds the `AnalysisStamp`, the payload's files and the COVERAGE: the sorted, merged ranges of
  grid indices stored. A request is a hit when the coverage holds every index of its window plus
  the kind's read margin; otherwise a job runs only the missing ranges, each with the kind's
  pre-roll, and the coverage grows. Payload files are written through a `.partial` and a rename,
  the marker last, all inside `CacheLedger.publish`, sorted keys, `.atomic`. The `AnalysisStamp`
  is the source's identity (`CacheStamp`'s size, modified second and duration; no path), the kind
  and its version (Vision request revisions inside it), a digest of the kind's parameters, the OS
  build, the compute device, and the reader's input: `raw`, or the conversion as
  `ConvertedThumbsStamp` records it (curve and gamut, or the LUT's path, size and second, or the
  HDR transfer; `fullRange`; a PQ peak). A stamp that differs in any field is a miss: the next
  store deletes the marker first, then the payload, and starts empty (§5.6's order). So relink,
  consolidate and `set_media_color` invalidate as they do every cache. Coordinates are normalised
  0…1 in the media's display orientation, origin top-left, and every answer carries the display
  width and height; times are media source ticks, so any clip, speed, ramp or reversal over the
  file reuses them through `SourceMap` and `ReverseMirror`.
- **CJ-23 — The frame reader.** `AnalysisFrames.swift` has two readers. The direct reader is an
  `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` over the first video track, decoded to 32BGRA, scaled to the kind's
  long edge and turned to display orientation from the track's orientation codes
  (`CompositionBuilder+Orientation.swift`). The converted reader is an
  `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` over `MediaImporter.oneClip`'s composition, rendered at
  the kind's size through step 0, so analysis sees what the person sees; `oneClip`
  (`MediaImporter+ThumbnailSource.swift:311`) loses `private` and nothing else in that file
  changes. A media whose picture converts (Camera Log, HLG, PQ) is read converted unless CJ-S2's
  rule 5 says otherwise for a kind; every other media is read direct. Frames are read in
  presentation order; each goes to the kind's per-frame callback, and a sample at k / rate takes
  the first frame whose presentation time is at or after it (VR's callbacks).
- **CJ-24 — `shots`, the first kind: hard cuts from a deterministic picture difference, no ML.**
  Each frame's signature (CJ-S4 picks it: a 32-bin luma histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, or a
  4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at long side 256) gives two stored values, d1, its L1 distance to the
  frame before, and d2, its distance to the frame two before; the kind's pre-roll is two frames.
  When answered, frame i is a cut when d1(i) ≥ T; d2(i + 1) ≥ T, so a single flash frame that
  returns to the shot is not a cut; and d1(i) is the largest d1 within m frames either side, ties
  to the earlier frame. A dissolve, whose frame-to-frame distances stay under T, is not a cut. T
  and m are CJ-S4's; the read margin is m + 1 frames each side. The same window answers the same
  cuts whatever was asked before.
- **CJ-25 — `get_media_analysis {media | clip, kind, from?, to?}` reads any kind, running or
  reusing it.** Exactly one of `media` and `clip`. With `media` the window defaults to the whole
  file; with `clip` it defaults to, and is clamped to, the clip's played source window, and each
  time is answered in clip ticks too, through the clip's source map and the reversal mirror. It
  runs off main (`creatorOffMainTools`) and waits with a bound fixed in CJ2a from CJ-S3's
  throughput, refusing past it with a sentence naming how much is covered. It answers `kind`, the
  source window, the display `size`, `cached` (true when nothing ran), the stamp, `run`
  (`queued_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at` in process uptime seconds, only when this call ran a
  job), and the kind's results: `shots` its `cuts`, `faces` its `samples`. An answer is capped by
  size; over the cap it is refused naming the largest window that fits. It is `get_transcript`'s
  counterpart for pictures and sounds, and every bet's kind answers through it (VR's `subjects`,
  CO's masks as chunk states, FC's `sound-events`).
- **CJ-26 — A canned analysis is honoured only for a proof.** A marker with `"canned": true`
  carries only the source identity, and is read only in a build with `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` launched
  with `-RCDevAnalysisCanned YES`, so a planner's proof is byte-exact on any Mac and
  Distribution never reads one.
- **CJ-27 — One Analyzing sheet for every kind (CJ2b).** A command whose analysis is not cached

- **CJ-28 — Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes and `split_at_shots {clips?}` (CJ2b).** The selected

### Spikes

Each rule is fixed here, before its run, and hashed at CJ0a. Instruments go in
`tools/proof/creator_spike/`; each run's `results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `creator-jobs.md`
as `rule_sha256` (CAM-2's precedent), and the verdict is recorded in the road map and in the
decision named. The analysis spikes are one set: CJ-S2 (Vision), CJ-S3 (the lane) and CJ-S4
(shots) hold the only rules for rate, size, device, log input, playback impact and shot
detection; VR1 and CO1 re-run their rows for their own kinds under the same rules.

- **CJ-S1 — The clip ceiling (at CJ6's head; decides CJ-9).** Question: how many clips can a
  project hold before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Projects of N = 4,096,
  8,192, 16,384 and 32,768 one-second media clips over four tracks of one media, generated as
  packages. N above 4,096 needs a scratch Release build with the cap raised, never committed.
  Measured: (1) `rc_project_apply` of `split` at the middle, median of 20; (2)
  `rc_project_from_json` plus `rc_composition_plan`; (3) `frame_recipe` at 20 random times,
  median; (4) over MCP, one `ripple_delete_ranges` of 100 ranges and its undo, each from the call
  to its answer; (5) after (4), the time until the next main-thread call (`get_project`) answers,
  which covers Swift's snapshot decode and the timeline's refresh; (6) after an edit, the time
  until `play_preview` composes its first frame, which covers `CompositionBuilder`'s rebuild; (7)
  the timeline's draw, from a probe built through `swift_build.py` that lays out and draws a
  `TimelineView` of N clips offscreen at the fit-all zoom and at the default zoom, median of 20;
  (8) the app's resident memory after 50 undo steps of `split`. **Rule:** N_max is the largest N
  for which (1) ≤ 50 ms, (2) ≤ 500 ms, (3) ≤ 2 ms, (4) applies and undoes in ≤ 1 s each, (5) ≤ 1 s,
  (6) ≤ 2 s, (7) ≤ 33 ms at both zooms, and (8) grows by at most a sixteenth of physical memory.
  N_max > 4,096 → CJ6 raises the ceiling to N_max; otherwise CJ-9 keeps 4,096 and CJ6 ends with
  the verdict and no code.
- **CJ-S2 — Vision on video (at CJ3's head; decides CJ-30 and CJ-32; replaces VR-S1's rules 1–4
  and CO-S1's device question).** Question: on which device, at what rate and size, and from which
  reader are Vision kinds deterministic, fast enough and accurate on this Mac? Inputs: the face
  fixtures of "Samples and fixtures", always; S-TH1, S-TH2, S-TH3 and S-TH4 when they exist.
  Measured: the cache bytes of three runs on each of CPU, GPU and Neural Engine; seconds per minute
  of source for decode, rectangles, and rectangles with landmarks, at long sides 720, 1280 and
  1920 and native; face recall (the share of samples, in the spans where a face is known present,
  with a box overlapping it) at each size; recall and reader cost raw against converted on each
  log or HLG sample; face share over S-TH1's first 60 s. **Rules:**
  1. **Device:** the fastest of the three whose three runs are byte-identical. If none is, the CPU
     when it meets rule 2's rate; otherwise the fastest, with every proof comparing against the
     cache only (E9's rule).
  2. **Rate:** 10 samples a second if decode plus rectangles plus landmarks run at least 3× real
     time on 1080p30 and 1.5× on 4K30 on the chosen device; else 5; else 2.5 (VR-S1's numbers).
  3. **Size:** the smallest long side of 720, 1280 and 1920 whose face recall is at least 98 % of
     recall at native size, on the small-face fixture and on S-TH1 when it exists.
  4. **Landmarks** stay in `faces` if they cost at most 2× rectangles alone; else mouth opening is
     a `mouths` kind on the same grid, built by SW8.
  5. **Log and HDR input:** the converted reader, unless on every log or HLG sample run raw recall
     is at least 98 % of converted recall AND the converted reader costs more than 1.5× the direct
     one per frame (CJ-S3's figure); then the face kinds read raw. With no such sample, converted.
  6. **Face share** on S-TH1's first 60 s, which its brief makes front-facing: below 95 % stops
     VR1 and SW8 until an amendment of CJ-30. CJ3 lands on the fixtures either way; without S-TH1
     the row is skipped by name and owed in CJ3's record.
  VR1 re-runs rules 1–3 and 5 for its `subjects` requests (human rectangles and saliency) with the
  same instrument, and keeps VR-S1's rules 5 and 6. CO1 runs rule 1 for its mask request.
- **CJ-S3 — The lane (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-21 and CJ-23; replaces CO-S4).** Question: what
  does decoding for analysis cost, does a second concurrent picture job pay, and does analysis
  cost playback? Measured on a 4K HEVC 10-bit HLG file and a 1080p H.264 file (synthetic, by
  `ffmpeg`, until S-TH4 exists): frames a second through the direct and the converted reader at
  long sides 256 and 1280; the total throughput of one job and of two; and `play_preview`'s
  composed frames over 20 s of a 1080p30 timeline idle, then with a `shots` job running.
  **Rules:** (a) **width:** 2 only if two jobs reach at least 1.5× one job's throughput; else 1.
  (b) **playback:** when composed frames with a job running fall by more than 2 % against idle,
  the picture queue pauses while any transport plays and resumes when none does (CJ-21). CJ3 (a
  `faces` job), VR1 (`subjects`) and CO1 (masks) each re-run (b) with their own job at their head;
  the first failure turns the pause on for every picture kind, recorded as an amendment of CJ-21.
  (c) **reader:** the converted reader for converting media and the direct one for the rest,
  unless CJ-S2's rule 5 says otherwise for a kind.
- **CJ-S4 — The shot signature (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-24; replaces VR-S2).** Question:
  which signature, threshold T and neighbourhood m find hard cuts inside one flattened clip?
  Candidates: a 32-bin luma histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, and a 4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at
  long side 256, both by L1 distance. Inputs: the shots fixture (known cuts, a dissolve, a white
  flash frame); a no-cut talking head (S-TH1, else ten minutes of the moving-still fixture); and
  flattened exports with known cut lists (the trial's exports when they exist, and always a
  synthetic one: a fixture project of 40 clips cut from four `testsrc` variants, exported by Frame
  Job, its cut list read from `get_project`). **Rule:** the signature and T with the highest
  recall on the flattened exports subject to at most one false cut per 10 minutes on the no-cut
  input, and m the largest of 4, 6, 8 and 12 frames that loses no true cut on the fixture. It
  passes at recall ≥ 98 % on the flattened exports. If no candidate passes, a 64 × 36 luma sum of
  absolute differences joins as a second signal and the run repeats; if that fails, CJ-24 ships
  with the measured recall stated in the guide.

**Lane plan (at most three lanes).** The lanes are split by the files they touch.

- **CJ0a** runs alone: it is the record every phase cites. Then **CJ0b, CJ0c and CJ0d run at
  once**, one per lane: their files are disjoint (the core; the menus, builder, document and
  dispatch; the snapshots, recipe, core edge, importer and reverse).
- **Lane A, words:** CJ0b → CJ1 → TX's phases → FC's phases. CJ1 changes the filler and caption
  sheets TX builds beside; FC needs TX's sentence spans and CJ1's gate. FC1 → FC2 is an
  independent chain inside FC and may move to whichever lane is idle first. TX's restore phase
  waits for CJ4 (lane C) and its bulk-cut phase for CJ6's verdict.

  stamp makes that a re-analysis rather than a mix, and proofs read caches. A change in Vision's
  request revisions is a kind-version bump.
- **Analysis competes with playback, export and `AUSoundIsolation`'s renders.** The picture queue
  is width 1 at `.utility` until CJ-S3 earns 2, and pauses while a transport plays when CJ-S3 (b)
  says so; each Vision kind's first phase re-measures with its own job. An export waiting on
  analysis (CO's masks) runs it at the same priority; a slower export is the accepted cost.
- **Log and HDR footage.** Faces and masks on a flat log picture may miss; CJ-S2's rule 5 picks
  the reader, and the stamp records it.
- **The fixture faces ship with macOS.** An OS update could remove or change the FlexAudio covers;
  the fixture script records their hashes and fails by name, and a new source is chosen in the
  phase's record.
- **The clip ceiling and undo memory.** Each edit keeps a whole project handle, so TX's word cuts
  and SW's switching press on memory and on Swift's per-edit decode and rebuild before they press
  on 4,096; CJ-S1 measures all three.
- **Five tabs at 280 pt** are 56 pt each; "Transcript" and "Document" may not fit (TX's decision).
- **The helper is shared with Rasterize.** FC's Claude ranking goes through `agent/` (AI-1), whose
  source is held byte-identical with Rasterize's; any new helper command is a change offered to
  both.
- **Ad-hoc signatures and TCC.** Input Monitoring, like Screen Recording, is lost at every
  `make app`; the granted tiers are manual checks.
- **Lanes collide on tables.** The frozen files' wiring lines, menus, `UIMenuTable.swift`,

- **The key rule may surprise.** A person with cached transcripts and no key keeps Remove Filler

- **Samples may not come.** Every phase runs on fixtures and skips real-sample rows by name; the

## Shared ground — CJ0 and shared infrastructure

This is the part of road map "creator-jobs" (`designs/creator-jobs.md`) that no single bet owns:
the scope and the record (CJ0a), the tolls (CJ0b, CJ0c, CJ0d), the key rule (CJ1), and the
infrastructure two or more bets would otherwise build twice or collide on (CJ2a, CJ2b, CJ3, CJ4,
CJ6). The six bets (TX transcript, CU cursor and recorder, VR vertical, FC find clips, SW switch
by speaker, CO cutout and layouts) are designed elsewhere. This section names what they build on,
reconciles what their sections assumed about it ("What the bets build on"), and sets the order
they run in. Line counts are `wc -l` at `d0661e5d` (main, 2026-11-01).

### Goal

A person gets two things from the shared phases directly, and everything else through the bets:

- **Honest AI controls.** A command that would send to Claude or AssemblyAI is greyed out when its
  key is missing, and its tooltip says which key and where to set it. An agent's call that would
  send is refused with the same sentence. Nothing falls back to a weaker on-device model. Results
  already paid for keep working without a key.
- **Split at Shot Changes.** Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes cuts a flattened video (a finished edit,
  a downloaded clip, a stream VOD) at each hard cut, as one undo step. It is the first command on
  the analysis lane and the lane's proof in real use.

For the bets, the shared phases provide: one gate for keys; one lane, one store, one reader and
one sheet for every analysis of pictures and sounds, with hard cuts and face samples as its first
kinds; source ranges on the three placement ops; a decided clip ceiling; the files at the cap cut
once, before three lanes reach for them; and the record (decisions, IDs, lanes, trial, samples).
A new project from a range of the timeline is FC1 and FC2's (bet 4), not a shared phase: only FC
uses it.

### Owner's answers applied

The owner's answers of 2026-11-01, verbatim: "Add all: 1-6. Remove all explicit non-goals. The
recorder can ask for input monitoring. Anything that requires significant AI should require that
the user has supplied a key. Otherwise disable. 'Cutting one real video per lead segment in Frame
Job alongside the first bet' OK. Create a full design, then we'll compact and begin."

The orchestrator's reading, which the owner can change:

- **"Add all: 1-6"** is all six bets of `designs/creator-survey.md` "The bets" (lines 173–356),

**CJ2a's and CJ2b's block (the analysis lane).**

- **CJ-20 — Analysis is a cache, made on demand.** It never runs at import, is never project
  state, and is never read by the composition plan or the frame recipe. A planner reads it and
  writes ordinary edits. A render drawn from it (CO's masks) is substituted by Swift, as a
  reversed file is (§5.6). So no analysis kind bumps the format. VR-10's on-demand rule is this
  one; the speech cache's import-time rule stands for speech.
- **CJ-21 — One lane, `AnalysisLane`, process-wide, with two queues.** A picture queue (decodes
  and Vision) and a sound queue (audio decodes and Sound Analysis), so a sound job never waits
  behind a face job. Each is its own `DispatchQueue` at `.utility`, never the cooperative pool and
  never `MediaCacheLane`; the picture queue's width is spike CJ-S3's (1 until it earns 2), the
  sound queue's 1. A job is a source, a window and the kinds asked for it; kinds that share a
  reader, a size and a grid decode once (VR's subjects and CJ3's faces). Jobs are wanted by owners
  — a document's command, a tool call, an export — as ramp audio's renders are (SR-12): a job
  nobody wants is cancelled, one wanted again while it runs is not, `wait` returns on landing,
  failure or cancellation, and an owner's `settled` runs on main. A job takes no `CachePass` and
  writes only through `CacheLedger.publish(in:for: nil)`, so an import pass and an analysis job of
  the same media never cancel or wait on each other. `-RCDevAnalysisHold <s>` (a build with
  `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` only) holds each job for s seconds before its first frame, polling
  cancellation every 50 ms, as `-RCDevRampRenderHold` does. When CJ-S3's playback rule turns it
  on, the picture queue pauses between frames while any transport plays and resumes when none
  does, through a new internal `BackgroundRender.anyPlaying` over its `transports`
  (`BackgroundRender.swift:71`).
- **CJ-22 — The store.** A kind's results for one source are a marker,
  `cache/analysis/<kind>/<source>.json`, and a payload folder, `cache/analysis/<kind>/<source>/`,
  holding whatever files the kind names (`faces` a `samples.bin`, `shots` a `frames.bin`, CO's
  masks one movie per chunk). `<source>` is the media id, or `<media id>r` for a kind that reads a
  media's reversed render (CO-4). A kind whose variants must coexist puts the variant in its
  name (`masks-standard`, `masks-best`). Every kind has a grid on source time — frames by
  presentation time (`shots`), samples at k / rate (`faces`, `subjects`), fixed chunks (masks),
  windows at k × hop (`sound-events`) — and stores per grid point only values that depend on that
  point's input and a fixed neighbourhood the kind names (`shots`' two previous frames), never on
  where a job began or on what else is cached. Thresholds over time, minimum lengths, smoothing
  and identity are applied when a request is answered, over the requested window. The marker
  holds the `AnalysisStamp`, the payload's files and the COVERAGE: the sorted, merged ranges of
  grid indices stored. A request is a hit when the coverage holds every index of its window plus
  the kind's read margin; otherwise a job runs only the missing ranges, each with the kind's
  pre-roll, and the coverage grows. Payload files are written through a `.partial` and a rename,
  the marker last, all inside `CacheLedger.publish`, sorted keys, `.atomic`. The `AnalysisStamp`
  is the source's identity (`CacheStamp`'s size, modified second and duration; no path), the kind
  and its version (Vision request revisions inside it), a digest of the kind's parameters, the OS
  build, the compute device, and the reader's input: `raw`, or the conversion as
  `ConvertedThumbsStamp` records it (curve and gamut, or the LUT's path, size and second, or the
  HDR transfer; `fullRange`; a PQ peak). A stamp that differs in any field is a miss: the next
  store deletes the marker first, then the payload, and starts empty (§5.6's order). So relink,
  consolidate and `set_media_color` invalidate as they do every cache. Coordinates are normalised
  0…1 in the media's display orientation, origin top-left, and every answer carries the display
  width and height; times are media source ticks, so any clip, speed, ramp or reversal over the
  file reuses them through `SourceMap` and `ReverseMirror`.
- **CJ-23 — The frame reader.** `AnalysisFrames.swift` has two readers. The direct reader is an
  `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` over the first video track, decoded to 32BGRA, scaled to the kind's
  long edge and turned to display orientation from the track's orientation codes
  (`CompositionBuilder+Orientation.swift`). The converted reader is an
  `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` over `MediaImporter.oneClip`'s composition, rendered at
  the kind's size through step 0, so analysis sees what the person sees; `oneClip`
  (`MediaImporter+ThumbnailSource.swift:311`) loses `private` and nothing else in that file
  changes. A media whose picture converts (Camera Log, HLG, PQ) is read converted unless CJ-S2's
  rule 5 says otherwise for a kind; every other media is read direct. Frames are read in
  presentation order; each goes to the kind's per-frame callback, and a sample at k / rate takes
  the first frame whose presentation time is at or after it (VR's callbacks).
- **CJ-24 — `shots`, the first kind: hard cuts from a deterministic picture difference, no ML.**
  Each frame's signature (CJ-S4 picks it: a 32-bin luma histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, or a
  4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at long side 256) gives two stored values, d1, its L1 distance to the
  frame before, and d2, its distance to the frame two before; the kind's pre-roll is two frames.
  When answered, frame i is a cut when d1(i) ≥ T; d2(i + 1) ≥ T, so a single flash frame that
  returns to the shot is not a cut; and d1(i) is the largest d1 within m frames either side, ties
  to the earlier frame. A dissolve, whose frame-to-frame distances stay under T, is not a cut. T
  and m are CJ-S4's; the read margin is m + 1 frames each side. The same window answers the same
  cuts whatever was asked before.
- **CJ-25 — `get_media_analysis {media | clip, kind, from?, to?}` reads any kind, running or
  reusing it.** Exactly one of `media` and `clip`. With `media` the window defaults to the whole
  file; with `clip` it defaults to, and is clamped to, the clip's played source window, and each
  time is answered in clip ticks too, through the clip's source map and the reversal mirror. It
  runs off main (`creatorOffMainTools`) and waits with a bound fixed in CJ2a from CJ-S3's
  throughput, refusing past it with a sentence naming how much is covered. It answers `kind`, the
  source window, the display `size`, `cached` (true when nothing ran), the stamp, `run`
  (`queued_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at` in process uptime seconds, only when this call ran a
  job), and the kind's results: `shots` its `cuts`, `faces` its `samples`. An answer is capped by
  size; over the cap it is refused naming the largest window that fits. It is `get_transcript`'s
  counterpart for pictures and sounds, and every bet's kind answers through it (VR's `subjects`,
  CO's masks as chunk states, FC's `sound-events`).
- **CJ-26 — A canned analysis is honoured only for a proof.** A marker with `"canned": true`
  carries only the source identity, and is read only in a build with `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` launched
  with `-RCDevAnalysisCanned YES`, so a planner's proof is byte-exact on any Mac and
  Distribution never reads one.
- **CJ-27 — One Analyzing sheet for every kind (CJ2b).** A command whose analysis is not cached
  shows it: "Analyzing" and the command's name, each media's progress, Stop. Stop withdraws the
  command's wants and lands nothing. A tool call shows no sheet and waits. The UI's words follow
  the menu's American verbs, as "Normalize" and "Synchronizing Audio" do: "Analyzing", "Analyze",
  and CO's status "Analyzing 42 %".
- **CJ-28 — Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes and `split_at_shots {clips?}` (CJ2b).** The selected
  media clips (else none: the item validates off) are split at each cut inside their played
  window, mapped to clip time through the source map, on the canvas grid, as one undo step "Split
  at Shot Changes". A cut within one frame of a clip's edge is dropped. Locked tracks and linked
  partners follow `split`'s own rules (AU-92). Over the clip ceiling, the whole command is refused
  before any split, naming how many clips it would add — every split counted with each linked
  partner it also cuts — and how many fit.

**CJ3's block (faces).**

- **CJ-30 — `faces`, the first machine-learning kind, for VR and SW.** Per sample of source time,
  every face: its box, confidence, roll and yaw (`VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest` revision 3); and,
  from `VNDetectFaceLandmarksRequest` revision 3 (the 76-point constellation) run on those
  observations, the mouth's inner-lip gap and outer-lip width, each over the face box's height in
  display pixels, so SW-81's ratio (gap over width) and a face-height ratio are both one division
  at read. Each request runs with a fresh `VNImageRequestHandler`; no stateful request is used
  (VR-4's rule). The rate, the read size and the device are CJ-S2's (first numbers: 10 a second,
  long side 1280). Landmarks stay in this kind unless CJ-S2's rule 4 moves them to a `mouths`
  kind, which SW8 then builds on the same grid.
- **CJ-31 — No identity is stored.** The store holds each sample's faces as Vision found them,

### Spikes

Each rule is fixed here, before its run, and hashed at CJ0a. Instruments go in
`tools/proof/creator_spike/`; each run's `results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `creator-jobs.md`
as `rule_sha256` (CAM-2's precedent), and the verdict is recorded in the road map and in the
decision named. The analysis spikes are one set: CJ-S2 (Vision), CJ-S3 (the lane) and CJ-S4
(shots) hold the only rules for rate, size, device, log input, playback impact and shot
detection; VR1 and CO1 re-run their rows for their own kinds under the same rules.

- **CJ-S1 — The clip ceiling (at CJ6's head; decides CJ-9).** Question: how many clips can a
  project hold before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Projects of N = 4,096,
  8,192, 16,384 and 32,768 one-second media clips over four tracks of one media, generated as
  packages. N above 4,096 needs a scratch Release build with the cap raised, never committed.
  Measured: (1) `rc_project_apply` of `split` at the middle, median of 20; (2)
  `rc_project_from_json` plus `rc_composition_plan`; (3) `frame_recipe` at 20 random times,
  median; (4) over MCP, one `ripple_delete_ranges` of 100 ranges and its undo, each from the call
  to its answer; (5) after (4), the time until the next main-thread call (`get_project`) answers,
  which covers Swift's snapshot decode and the timeline's refresh; (6) after an edit, the time
  until `play_preview` composes its first frame, which covers `CompositionBuilder`'s rebuild; (7)
  the timeline's draw, from a probe built through `swift_build.py` that lays out and draws a
  `TimelineView` of N clips offscreen at the fit-all zoom and at the default zoom, median of 20;
  (8) the app's resident memory after 50 undo steps of `split`. **Rule:** N_max is the largest N
  for which (1) ≤ 50 ms, (2) ≤ 500 ms, (3) ≤ 2 ms, (4) applies and undoes in ≤ 1 s each, (5) ≤ 1 s,
  (6) ≤ 2 s, (7) ≤ 33 ms at both zooms, and (8) grows by at most a sixteenth of physical memory.
  N_max > 4,096 → CJ6 raises the ceiling to N_max; otherwise CJ-9 keeps 4,096 and CJ6 ends with
  the verdict and no code.
- **CJ-S2 — Vision on video (at CJ3's head; decides CJ-30 and CJ-32; replaces VR-S1's rules 1–4
  and CO-S1's device question).** Question: on which device, at what rate and size, and from which
  reader are Vision kinds deterministic, fast enough and accurate on this Mac? Inputs: the face
  fixtures of "Samples and fixtures", always; S-TH1, S-TH2, S-TH3 and S-TH4 when they exist.
  Measured: the cache bytes of three runs on each of CPU, GPU and Neural Engine; seconds per minute
  of source for decode, rectangles, and rectangles with landmarks, at long sides 720, 1280 and
  1920 and native; face recall (the share of samples, in the spans where a face is known present,
  with a box overlapping it) at each size; recall and reader cost raw against converted on each
  log or HLG sample; face share over S-TH1's first 60 s. **Rules:**
  1. **Device:** the fastest of the three whose three runs are byte-identical. If none is, the CPU
     when it meets rule 2's rate; otherwise the fastest, with every proof comparing against the
     cache only (E9's rule).
  2. **Rate:** 10 samples a second if decode plus rectangles plus landmarks run at least 3× real
     time on 1080p30 and 1.5× on 4K30 on the chosen device; else 5; else 2.5 (VR-S1's numbers).
  3. **Size:** the smallest long side of 720, 1280 and 1920 whose face recall is at least 98 % of
     recall at native size, on the small-face fixture and on S-TH1 when it exists.
  4. **Landmarks** stay in `faces` if they cost at most 2× rectangles alone; else mouth opening is
     a `mouths` kind on the same grid, built by SW8.
  5. **Log and HDR input:** the converted reader, unless on every log or HLG sample run raw recall
     is at least 98 % of converted recall AND the converted reader costs more than 1.5× the direct
     one per frame (CJ-S3's figure); then the face kinds read raw. With no such sample, converted.
  6. **Face share** on S-TH1's first 60 s, which its brief makes front-facing: below 95 % stops
     VR1 and SW8 until an amendment of CJ-30. CJ3 lands on the fixtures either way; without S-TH1
     the row is skipped by name and owed in CJ3's record.
  VR1 re-runs rules 1–3 and 5 for its `subjects` requests (human rectangles and saliency) with the
  same instrument, and keeps VR-S1's rules 5 and 6. CO1 runs rule 1 for its mask request.
- **CJ-S3 — The lane (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-21 and CJ-23; replaces CO-S4).** Question: what
  does decoding for analysis cost, does a second concurrent picture job pay, and does analysis
  cost playback? Measured on a 4K HEVC 10-bit HLG file and a 1080p H.264 file (synthetic, by
  `ffmpeg`, until S-TH4 exists): frames a second through the direct and the converted reader at
  long sides 256 and 1280; the total throughput of one job and of two; and `play_preview`'s
  composed frames over 20 s of a 1080p30 timeline idle, then with a `shots` job running.
  **Rules:** (a) **width:** 2 only if two jobs reach at least 1.5× one job's throughput; else 1.
  (b) **playback:** when composed frames with a job running fall by more than 2 % against idle,
  the picture queue pauses while any transport plays and resumes when none does (CJ-21). CJ3 (a
  `faces` job), VR1 (`subjects`) and CO1 (masks) each re-run (b) with their own job at their head;
  the first failure turns the pause on for every picture kind, recorded as an amendment of CJ-21.
  (c) **reader:** the converted reader for converting media and the direct one for the rest,
  unless CJ-S2's rule 5 says otherwise for a kind.
- **CJ-S4 — The shot signature (at CJ2a's head; decides CJ-24; replaces VR-S2).** Question:
  which signature, threshold T and neighbourhood m find hard cuts inside one flattened clip?
  Candidates: a 32-bin luma histogram of a 64 × 36 downscale, and a 4 × 4 × 4 colour histogram at
  long side 256, both by L1 distance. Inputs: the shots fixture (known cuts, a dissolve, a white
  flash frame); a no-cut talking head (S-TH1, else ten minutes of the moving-still fixture); and
  flattened exports with known cut lists (the trial's exports when they exist, and always a
  synthetic one: a fixture project of 40 clips cut from four `testsrc` variants, exported by Frame
  Job, its cut list read from `get_project`). **Rule:** the signature and T with the highest
  recall on the flattened exports subject to at most one false cut per 10 minutes on the no-cut
  input, and m the largest of 4, 6, 8 and 12 frames that loses no true cut on the fixture. It
  passes at recall ≥ 98 % on the flattened exports. If no candidate passes, a 64 × 36 luma sum of
  absolute differences joins as a second signal and the run repeats; if that fails, CJ-24 ships
  with the measured recall stated in the guide.

**How Vision-dependent proofs stay deterministic.** (1) A planner's rows run on canned analyses
and assert bytes. (2) Vision's rows on fixtures and real samples assert tolerances fixed before
the run, never exact numbers. (3) A determinism row compares two runs on the pinned device, byte
for byte. (4) A proof compares against the cache, never against a recomputation. (5) Every stamp
carries the OS build, the compute device and the reader's input, and every results file records
all three. (6) Stored values depend on one grid point, so an answer never depends on call order
(CJ2a's A9). (7) What only a person can judge — whether a reframe, a cutout or a switch looks
right on real footage — is a JOB row.

### Risks

- **Vision moves under the app.** An OS update or another compute device changes the numbers; the
  stamp makes that a re-analysis rather than a mix, and proofs read caches. A change in Vision's
  request revisions is a kind-version bump.
- **Analysis competes with playback, export and `AUSoundIsolation`'s renders.** The picture queue
  is width 1 at `.utility` until CJ-S3 earns 2, and pauses while a transport plays when CJ-S3 (b)
  says so; each Vision kind's first phase re-measures with its own job. An export waiting on
  analysis (CO's masks) runs it at the same priority; a slower export is the accepted cost.
- **Log and HDR footage.** Faces and masks on a flat log picture may miss; CJ-S2's rule 5 picks
  the reader, and the stamp records it.
- **The fixture faces ship with macOS.** An OS update could remove or change the FlexAudio covers;
  the fixture script records their hashes and fails by name, and a new source is chosen in the
  phase's record.
- **The clip ceiling and undo memory.** Each edit keeps a whole project handle, so TX's word cuts
  and SW's switching press on memory and on Swift's per-edit decode and rebuild before they press
  on 4,096; CJ-S1 measures all three.
- **Five tabs at 280 pt** are 56 pt each; "Transcript" and "Document" may not fit (TX's decision).
- **The helper is shared with Rasterize.** FC's Claude ranking goes through `agent/` (AI-1), whose
  source is held byte-identical with Rasterize's; any new helper command is a change offered to
  both.
- **Ad-hoc signatures and TCC.** Input Monitoring, like Screen Recording, is lost at every
  `make app`; the granted tiers are manual checks.
- **Lanes collide on tables.** The frozen files' wiring lines, menus, `UIMenuTable.swift`,
  `inventory.json`, `menus-and-shortcuts.md`, the decision file, the spec index's Lines cells and
  the pinned counts all take rows from three lanes; the integrator resolves them one landing at a
  time (CJ-6, CJ-8 (g)), and T8 moves the busiest two out of a frozen file.
- **Provisional format numbers.** CU, SW, CO and VR (linked versions) each may bump; renumbering at

  brand kit, the publish polish slice, `search_media`, merging the tutorials, optical-flow slow
  motion, WebVTT import.

  or account (C2, #125 stays iced), and the Keychain for keys (R6-5's measured reason stands).

  graphics, third-party Audio Unit hosting, stabilisation, motion blur, optical-flow retiming,

content.content:
## Shared ground — CJ0 and shared infrastructure

This is the part of road map "creator-jobs" (`designs/creator-jobs.md`) that no single bet owns:
the scope and the record (CJ0a), the tolls (CJ0b, CJ0c, CJ0d), the key rule (CJ1), and the
infrastructure two or more bets would otherwise build twice or collide on (CJ2a, CJ2b, CJ3, CJ4,
CJ6). The six bets (TX transcript, CU cursor and recorder, VR vertical, FC find clips, SW switch
by speaker, CO cutout and layouts) are designed elsewhere. This section names what they build on,
reconciles what their sections assumed about it ("What the bets build on"), and sets the order

For the bets, the shared phases provide: one gate for keys; one lane, one store, one reader and
one sheet for every analysis of pictures and sounds, with hard cuts and face samples as its first
kinds; source ranges on the three placement ops; a decided clip ceiling; the files at the cap cut
once, before three lanes reach for them; and the record (decisions, IDs, lanes, trial, samples).
A new project from a range of the timeline is FC1 and FC2's (bet 4), not a shared phase: only FC
uses it.

### Owner's answers applied
  (`EditorViewController.swift:26`), so a fifth tab is 56 pt wide at the minimum.
- `RecorderStatusItem.swift:7–13` records why the recorder has no global hotkey: it would need
  Input Monitoring or Accessibility. The recorder's grants live in `RecordingSetup.swift`'s
  `// MARK: - The grants` (249–398).
- The compositor binds `texture(0)`…`texture(3)` (source, matte coverage, look, curves;
  `Compositor.metal`); `texture(4)` and up are free. `LayerUniforms` grows by groups of four.

**Dispatch and the pinned counts.**

- The frozen `AgentServer.swift` (807) holds `productOffMainTools` (`:108–113`), merged with the
  dev tools' set at `:115` (`offMainTools = productOffMainTools.union(devOffMainTools)`), the
- **CJ-32 — The compute device is pinned and recorded in the stamp.** Every supported Mac is
  Apple silicon (spec §1) and has a CPU, a GPU and a Neural Engine; CJ-S2's rule 1 picks one for
  every Vision kind, and a request is pinned to it (`setComputeDevice(_:for:)`). A proof compares
  against the cache, never against a recomputation (E9's rule).

**CJ4's block (source ranges).**

- **CJ-40 — `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` take an optional `source_in` (media
  source ticks, default 0) and an optional `duration` (timeline ticks, default the rest of the
  file from `source_in`).** `source_in` is snapped to the canvas grid, as a front trim from 0
  would place the in point. Refused, each in its own sentence: `source_in` below 0 or at or past
  the file's last frame; either argument on a still or an image media ("a still has no source
  window"); a `duration` longer than the window, naming the longest that fits
  (`source_window.rs`'s `longest_duration_on_grid_of`). A `duration` of 0 or less is invalid
  input. `insert_clip` shifts by the placed duration. No format change: the stored clip is the
  one a placement and two trims make today.

**CJ6's block (the clip ceiling; only if CJ-S1 earns it).**

- **CJ-60 — `MAX_CLIPS` and `RC_MAX_CLIPS` rise together to CJ-S1's N, with no format bump.** The
  file's shape is unchanged. An older build refuses a file over its own ceiling with "too many

|---|---|---|---|
| CJ0a | serial, first | The scope lifted, the record opened, the spec's two splits | — |
| CJ0b | A | The core's tolls T1–T4 | CJ0a |
| CJ0c | B | The app's tolls T5–T8 | CJ0a |
| CJ0d | C | The app's tolls T11–T17 | CJ0a |
| CJ1 | A | AI commands greyed with a tooltip naming the missing key; tools refuse in that sentence | CJ0a |
| CJ4 | C | Agents place part of a file in one call | CJ0b (T1, T4) |
| CJ6 | C | Larger projects, only if CJ-S1 earns it | CJ0a |
| CJ2a | C | `get_media_analysis` with `shots`; the analysis lane, store and reader | CJ0c (T8) |
| CJ2b | C | Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes; the Analyzing sheet | CJ2a, CJ0c (T5) |
| CJ3 | C | Face samples for agents, VR and SW | CJ2a |

CJ5 is retired: a new project from a range is FC1 and FC2's (bet 4), the only bet that uses it.

**Lane plan (at most three lanes).** The lanes are split by the files they touch.

- **CJ0a** runs alone: it is the record every phase cites. Then **CJ0b, CJ0c and CJ0d run at
  once**, one per lane: their files are disjoint (the core; the menus, builder, document and
  dispatch; the snapshots, recipe, core edge, importer and reverse).
- **Lane A, words:** CJ0b → CJ1 → TX's phases → FC's phases. CJ1 changes the filler and caption
  sheets TX builds beside; FC needs TX's sentence spans and CJ1's gate. FC1 → FC2 is an
  independent chain inside FC and may move to whichever lane is idle first. TX's restore phase
  waits for CJ4 (lane C) and its bulk-cut phase for CJ6's verdict.
- **Lane B, recorder and presenter:** CJ0c → CU's phases → CO's phases. Both touch the recorder,
  the landing, the recipe layer and the compositor, so one lane keeps them serial. CU waits for
  CJ0b and CJ0d to land; CO's mask kind waits for CJ2a, its sheet for CJ2b, which land while CU
  runs.
- **Lane C, shared and picture:** CJ0d → CJ4 → CJ6 → CJ2a → CJ2b → CJ3 → VR's phases → SW's
  phases. The small shared phases come first because lanes A and B wait on them; VR needs CJ2b's
  sheet and `shots` and CJ3's faces; SW needs CJ3's faces and CJ6's verdict, and comes last, as
  the lead order puts video podcasts last.
- **The trial** (CJ-5) runs beside lane A: T1 and T2 cut when TX1 starts, again at TX's close.
- **Order across bets:** TX, CU first (lanes A, B), then CO (lane B) — the three lead bets —
  while lane C lays the shared ground and then builds VR and SW; FC follows TX in lane A. If the
  trial says otherwise, the integrator reorders by an amendment to CJ-2.

#### CJ0a — the scope and the record

- **What a person gets:** nothing in the app. The road map, its decisions and the spec's scope.
- **Record:** `designs/creator-jobs.md` opened from the designers' sections, with this section's
  `edit_described.rs`: `TITLE_FONT` and `TITLE_CONTENT` (67–72), `Described` (78–84) and
  `add_text_clip`, `add_shape_clip`, `add_described_clip` (233–387) in a new `impl Project` block.
  `DEFAULT_CLIP_DURATION` (62) stays, because `whole_media_length` (`:156`) reads it, and becomes
  `pub(crate)` for `add_described_clip`. `edit_adjustment.rs:63` and `edit_graphic.rs:34` change
  their `use crate::edit_clip::Described` to `crate::edit_described::Described`; `lib.rs` gains
  `mod edit_described;`. CJ4 edits `add_clip`; SW may need a split that leaves a linked partner
  alone.
- **Map entries:** `core/CLAUDE.md` gains `op_rows.rs`, `model_media.rs`, `recipe_hash.rs`,
  `edit_described.rs`; spec §7.10's rows; each file's "Named next cuts" entry in
  fixture).
- **Manual checks:** none (a person judges faces through VR and SW).
- **Depends on:** CJ2a.
- **Questions for the owner:** none expected; CJ-S2 decides device, rate, size and reader.

#### CJ4 — source ranges on the placement ops

- **What a person gets:** nothing directly; TX's restore and FC's placing of a found moment use
  it. An agent places part of a file in one call.
- **Core:** `add_clip` (`edit_clip.rs`, after T4), `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip`
  (`edit_insert.rs`, 154) take `source_in` and `duration` (CJ-40), through `source_window.rs`'s
  bound and mover; `op_rows.rs` (after T1): three rows gain two optional arguments; `edit.rs`'s
  doc table states what an absent one means. New `core/tests/source_range.rs`. No format change.
- **FFI:** none.
- **Swift:** `ReelOps.swift` (exempt): the three typed builders take the two optionals;
  `AgentServer+Clips.swift` (477) and the edge handlers pass them. No UI door of its own.
- **MCP mirror:** the three op tools print the new arguments from the core's table; one sentence
  of prose each in `AgentCatalog+Clips.swift` (574).
- **Docs:** spec §6 (`06b-edit-operations-clips.md`, 482: the three rows — it splits into a
  lettered file if this takes it past ~500), §7.9a; `docs/guide/mcp.md`.
- **Acceptance:** `make gate`; `cargo test --release --test source_range`;
  `source_range_proof.py` PASS against Release.
- **Proof rows:** R1 `add_clip` with both arguments: the clip's `in` and duration read back through
  `get_project`; R2 `insert_clip` shifts later clips by the placed duration; R3 each refusal's
  sentence (past the last frame, a still, a duration past the window naming the longest);
  R4 an export of a range-placed clip equals the export of the same clip made by `add_clip` plus
  two trims, sample for sample (ffmpeg PCM).
- **Mutants:** `source_in` unchecked against the file (R3); a long duration clamped instead of
  refused (R3); `source_in` not snapped (R1); `insert_clip` shifting by the file's length (R2).
- **Manual checks:** none.
- **Depends on:** CJ0b (T1, T4).
- **Questions for the owner:** a duration past the window — refuse naming the longest that fits,
  or clamp? *Recommended: refuse*, as a speed ramp's overrun names the rate that fits; an agent
  learns the bound instead of getting a shorter clip in silence.

#### CJ6 — the clip ceiling

- **What a person gets:** projects with more cuts, if the measurement allows: a long talk cut word
  by word, or a two-hour podcast switched every few seconds.
- **Spike first:** CJ-S1 runs at the phase's head. If its verdict keeps 4,096, the phase ends with
  the verdict recorded in CJ-9 and no code.

- The six bets themselves, and every analysis kind only one bet needs: subjects (VR1), person
  masks (CO1), sound events (FC3), cursor data (CU). Each lives in this section's store and lane.
- A new project from a range: FC1 and FC2's.
- The survey's next tier: Proposals and Recipes, Punch in on cuts, a source viewer with skimming,
  In and Out on media and favourite ranges (CJ4 is only the op arguments), caption styles and a
  brand kit, the publish polish slice, `search_media`, merging the tutorials, optical-flow slow
  motion, WebVTT import.
- Everything in the survey's "Not worth chasing" table.
- An on-device language model (FoundationModels), an on-device filler pass, a Frame Job-run relay
  or account (C2, #125 stays iced), and the Keychain for keys (R6-5's measured reason stands).

content.content:
### Goal

A person gets two things from the shared phases directly, and everything else through the bets:

- **Honest AI controls.** A command that would send to Claude or AssemblyAI is greyed out when its
  key is missing, and its tooltip says which key and where to set it. An agent's call that would
  send is refused with the same sentence. Nothing falls back to a weaker on-device model. Results
  already paid for keep working without a key.
- **Split at Shot Changes.** Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes cuts a flattened video (a finished edit,
  a downloaded clip, a stream VOD) at each hard cut, as one undo step. It is the first command on
  the analysis lane and the lane's proof in real use.

For the bets, the shared phases provide: one gate for keys; one lane, one store, one reader and
one sheet for every analysis of pictures and sounds, with hard cuts and face samples as its first
kinds; a decided clip ceiling; the files at the cap cut once, before three lanes reach for them;
and the record (decisions, IDs, lanes, trial, samples). A new project from a range of the
timeline is FC1 and FC2's (bet 4), not a shared phase: only FC uses it. Source ranges on the
placement ops are the survey's next tier, and no bet uses them (CJ4 retired).

### Owner's answers applied
1339

phases.title: The scope and the record
phases.gets: Nothing in the app. This phase opens the road map. It records CJ-1…CJ-9 plus the bet-level decisions VR-1…VR-7, SW-1 and TX-70, adds the amendment lines (recording.md, CAM-1, AU-2, G-1, R5-1, GR-1, GR-20, GR-27…GR-30, R6-17, AI-8, TR-10), rewrites §1 and §2, makes the two doc-only spec splits (T9: 07.9a → 07.9e; T10: 04.3b → 04.3d), and hashes every spike rule.
questions_for_owner: Merge into main per phase or at the road map's close? Recommended: per phase.
Lift §2's Left out list with §1's? Recommended: yes.
Real samples in tools/proof/media/creator/ (gitignored), rows in samples/README.md; which samples will you record and when? No phase waits for one.
Survey decision 8 (multi-stream 4K, multi-hour) as SW's first spike SW-S2? Recommended: yes.

'Remove all explicit non-goals' read literally also lifts GR-20, GR-27…GR-30, third-party Audio Unit hosting (AU-2) and scripting beyond graphics (G-1). Read it that way? Recommended: yes. It builds none of them, and a road map that would build one asks first.

phases.title: The core's tolls T1–T4
phases.gets: Nothing visible. Four pure moves, each gated alone: op_table.rs rows → op_rows.rs; model.rs media types → model_media.rs; recipe.rs content hash → recipe_hash.rs (this is CO0's T3); edit_clip.rs described clips → edit_described.rs (DEFAULT_CLIP_DURATION stays and is widened; two `use` lines change).

phases.title: The app's tolls T5–T8: menus, builder, document, dispatch
phases.gets: Nothing visible. View menu → AppDelegate+ViewMenu.swift (viewMenu widened). The held last frame → CompositionBuilder+HeldFrame.swift (moves a TYPECHECK_BASELINE row and the root CLAUDE.md sentence). Reverse machinery → ProjectDocument+Reverse.swift. New AgentServer+CreatorJobs.swift with creatorHandlers, creatorOffMainTools and withCreatorHandlers, merged by the frozen file's two existing lines.

phases.title: The app's tolls T11–T17: snapshots, recipe, core edge, importer, reverse
phases.gets: Nothing visible. These are the cuts CU0, CO0 and SW expect of CJ0. ProjectSnapshot.swift gives up VideoProps → VideoProps.swift, the Clips MARK → ClipSnapshot.swift and the Tracks MARK → TrackSnapshot.swift. FrameRecipe.swift's matte types → FrameRecipe+Mattes.swift. ReelCore.swift takes its named doc cut, leaving room for CU1's ReelCursor.check. MediaImporter.swift's frames-loop write → +Thumbnails. ReverseRenderer's Settings → ReverseRenderer+Settings.swift.

phases.title: The key gate (ModelKeys)
phases.gets: With no key, every command that would send to Claude or AssemblyAI is greyed, with a tooltip naming the key and where to set it, and saving a key enables it at once. Tools refuse in their own order with the same sentence; transcribe_for_fillers on a ready media still answers. Generate Captions' engine item stays enabled and Start carries the tooltip. There is no dispatch line, no memo, and the store is injected. The parity check gains a sixth part.
phases.needs_key: none to build; proofs use dummy keys against stand-in servers

phases.title: The analysis lane, its store and reader, and shots
phases.gets: get_media_analysis {media | clip, kind, from?, to?} with the shots kind. AnalysisLane has picture and sound queues (no CachePass), plus -RCDevAnalysisHold and the pause rule. AnalysisStore stores cache/analysis/<kind>/<source>.json plus a payload folder, with coverage on the kind's grid and state-free values. AnalysisStamp includes the reader's input. Readers: direct, and converted via AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput over oneClip, which is widened. Shots store d1/d2 per frame and apply the threshold, flash and local-max rules at read.

phases.title: The Analyzing sheet and Split at Shot Changes
phases.gets: Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes: the Analyzing sheet (with Stop), then one undo step that splits the clip at every hard cut inside its played window, mapped through the source map. The ceiling check counts linked partners. Adds split_at_shots {clips?}.

phases.title: Face samples
phases.gets: get_media_analysis kind faces. Per sample: box, confidence, roll and yaw (rectangles r3), plus the inner-lip gap and mouth width over box height (landmarks r3). No ids are stored, the device is pinned and recorded in the stamp, and the fixtures use the macOS-shipped FlexAudio covers. This is what VR and SW build on.

phases.title: The clip ceiling (CJ-S1 first; code only if earned)
phases.gets: CJ-S1 runs at the head and covers the core, MCP, main-thread decode, rebuild, timeline draw and memory. If N_max is above 4,096, MAX_CLIPS and RC_MAX_CLIPS rise to N with no format bump. Otherwise the verdict is recorded and no code is written. Runs just before SW, its only consumer.
questions_for_owner: Raise MAX_CLIPS to the spike's N if it passes? Recommended: yes.

spikes.question: How many clips can a project hold before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Measured in the core, over MCP, on the main thread after an edit, in the rebuild, in the timeline draw, and in memory.
spikes.rule: N_max is the largest N in {4096, 8192, 16384, 32768} that passes every limit: split apply ≤ 50 ms; from_json + plan ≤ 500 ms; recipe ≤ 2 ms; ripple_delete_ranges of 100 ranges and its undo ≤ 1 s each; next main-thread call ≤ 1 s; first composed frame after an edit ≤ 2 s; timeline draw ≤ 33 ms at both zooms; memory growth after 50 undos ≤ 1/16 of physical. If N_max > 4096, CJ6 raises the ceiling; otherwise it stays 4096 and CJ6 ships no code.

spikes.question: On which device, at what rate and size, and from which reader are Vision kinds deterministic, fast enough and accurate? Run at CJ3's head; it replaces VR-S1 rules 1–4 and CO-S1's device question, and VR1 and CO1 re-run it for their kinds.
spikes.rule: (1) Device: the fastest of CPU/GPU/ANE whose three runs are byte-identical; else the CPU if it meets the rate; else the fastest, with cache-only proofs. (2) Rate: 10/s if decode + rectangles + landmarks run ≥ 3× real time at 1080p30 and ≥ 1.5× at 4K30; else 5; else 2.5. (3) Size: the smallest of 720/1280/1920 whose face recall is ≥ 98 % of native. (4) Landmarks stay in faces if they cost ≤ 2× rectangles; else a mouths kind built by SW8. (5) Log/HDR: converted, unless raw recall is ≥ 98 % of converted on every log/HLG sample AND the converted reader costs > 1.5× the direct one. (6) Face share on S-TH1's first 60 s below 95 % stops VR1 and SW8 until CJ-30 is amended; without S-TH1, skipped by name.

spikes.question: What does decoding for analysis cost, does a second picture job pay, and does analysis cost playback? Run at CJ2a's head; it replaces CO-S4, and its row (b) is re-run by CJ3, VR1 and CO1.
spikes.rule: (a) Width 2 only if two jobs reach ≥ 1.5× one job's throughput. (b) If composed frames fall by more than 2 % against idle while a job runs, the picture queue pauses while any transport plays; the first kind to fail turns the pause on for all. (c) The converted reader for converting media and the direct one otherwise, unless CJ-S2 rule 5 says otherwise.

spikes.question: Which signature, threshold T and neighbourhood m find hard cuts in a flattened clip? Run at CJ2a's head; it replaces VR-S2.
spikes.rule: Pick the signature (32-bin luma of 64×36, or 4×4×4 colour at long side 256) and T with the highest recall on flattened exports, with at most one false cut per 10 min on a no-cut talking head. m is the largest of 4/6/8/12 frames that loses no true cut on the fixture. It passes at recall ≥ 98 %. Otherwise add luma SAD as a second signal and repeat; if that fails, ship with the measured recall stated in the guide.

shared_needs: The FC section (fc.md) changes: FC1 and FC2 own keep_range and New Project from Range whole (CJ5 is retired). FC1 also owes the ninth ReelOp.documentLevelNames entry, app/CLAUDE.md's 'eight names', spec §6a's 'Ten ops', and FC-13's argued opsWithoutTools line. FC2's handler and off-main entry go in creatorHandlers/creatorOffMainTools, not AgentServer.swift. FC2's range-export comparison keeps ducks, levellers and transitions away from the range edges.

The VR section (vr.md) changes: 'CJ1' means CJ2a. VR1 builds no lane, ledger change, ShotSignature or get_subjects. Its subjects kind (human rectangles and saliency only) goes in cache/analysis/subjects/ through AnalysisStore and is answered by get_media_analysis {clip, kind: "subjects"}. Faces come from CJ3. Shots come from CJ2a (VR-14 and VR-S2 are replaced by CJ-24 and CJ-S4). Boxes are stored 0…1 with the display size; association stays VR-5's core arithmetic. VR-S1 keeps only rules 5–6 and re-runs CJ-S2 rules 1–3 and 5 plus CJ-S3 (b) at VR1's head. UI strings say 'Analyzing'.

The CO section (co.md) changes: CO1 builds no VideoAnalysisLane. Masks are kind masks-<quality> in cache/analysis/, with chunk movies in the payload folder and reversed-render sources keyed <media id>r. AnalysisStamp replaces ReverseCache's digest, so no path is stored. CO-S4 becomes CJ-S3 (b). CO0's T1 and T3 are paid by CJ0d T11–T13 and CJ0b T3. Status reads 'Analyzing 42 %'. Manual checks keep JOB-60…69.

The SW section (sw.md) changes: its multicam scope draft is recorded as SW-1 at CJ0a. SW-80's landmarks request is CJ3's faces, at CJ-S2's rate. risks: Vision output changes with the OS or the compute device. The stamp records the OS build, the device and the reader's input, so a change triggers re-analysis, and proofs compare against the cache.

Analysis competes with playback, export and AUSoundIsolation renders. The picture queue runs at width 1 and .utility until CJ-S3 says otherwise, and pauses while a transport plays if CJ-S3 (b) fails for any kind.
Faces and masks may miss on log and HDR footage. CJ-S2 rule 5 picks the reader, and the stamp records it.

Undo memory and Swift's per-edit decode and rebuild may limit clip count before 4,096 does. CJ-S1 measures all three.

The helper is shared with Rasterize, so FC's ranking command is a change offered to both apps.

phases.title: The analysis lane, its store and reader, and shots
phases.gets: get_media_analysis {media | clip, kind, from?, to?} with the shots kind. AnalysisLane has picture and sound queues (no CachePass), plus -RCDevAnalysisHold and the pause rule. phases.title: The Analyzing sheet and Split at Shot Changes
phases.gets: Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes: the Analyzing sheet (with Stop), then one undo step that splits the clip at every hard cut inside its played window, mapped through the source map. The ceiling check counts linked partners. Adds split_at_shots {clips?}.

phases.title: Face samples
phases.gets: get_media_analysis kind faces. Per sample: box, confidence, roll and yaw (rectangles r3), plus the inner-lip gap and mouth width over box height (landmarks r3). phases.title: The clip ceiling (CJ-S1 first; code only if earned)
phases.gets: CJ-S1 runs at the head and covers the core, MCP, main-thread decode, rebuild, timeline draw and memory. If N_max is above 4,096, MAX_CLIPS and RC_MAX_CLIPS rise to N with no format bump. Otherwise the verdict is recorded and no code is written. Runs just before SW, its only consumer.
questions_for_owner: Raise MAX_CLIPS to the spike's N if it passes? Recommended: yes.

spikes.question: How many clips can a project hold before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Measured in the core, over MCP, on the main thread after an edit, in the rebuild, in the timeline draw, and in memory.
spikes.rule: N_max is the largest N in {4096, 8192, 16384, 32768} that passes every limit: split apply ≤ 50 ms; from_json + plan ≤ 500 ms; recipe ≤ 2 ms; ripple_delete_ranges of 100 ranges and its undo ≤ 1 s each; next main-thread call ≤ 1 s; first composed frame after an edit ≤ 2 s; timeline draw ≤ 33 ms at both zooms; memory growth after 50 undos ≤ 1/16 of physical. If N_max > 4096, CJ6 raises the ceiling; otherwise it stays 4096 and CJ6 ships no code.

spikes.question: On which device, at what rate and size, and from which reader are Vision kinds deterministic, fast enough and accurate? Run at CJ3's head; it replaces VR-S1 rules 1–4 and CO-S1's device question, and VR1 and CO1 re-run it for their kinds.
spikes.rule: (1) Device: the fastest of CPU/GPU/ANE whose three runs are byte-identical; else the CPU if it meets the rate; else the fastest, with cache-only proofs. (2) Rate: 10/s if decode + rectangles + landmarks run ≥ 3× real time at 1080p30 and ≥ 1.5× at 4K30; else 5; else 2.5. (3) Size: the smallest of 720/1280/1920 whose face recall is ≥ 98 % of native. (4) Landmarks stay in faces if they cost ≤ 2× rectangles; else a mouths kind built by SW8. (5) Log/HDR: converted, unless raw recall is ≥ 98 % of converted on every log/HLG sample AND the converted reader costs > 1.5× the direct one. (6) Face share on S-TH1's first 60 s below 95 % stops VR1 and SW8 until CJ-30 is amended; without S-TH1, skipped by name.

spikes.question: What does decoding for analysis cost, does a second picture job pay, and does analysis cost playback? Run at CJ2a's head; it replaces CO-S4, and its row (b) is re-run by CJ3, VR1 and CO1.
spikes.rule: (a) Width 2 only if two jobs reach ≥ 1.5× one job's throughput. (b) If composed frames fall by more than 2 % against idle while a job runs, the picture queue pauses while any transport plays; the first kind to fail turns the pause on for all. (c) The converted reader for converting media and the direct one otherwise, unless CJ-S2 rule 5 says otherwise.

spikes.question: Which signature, threshold T and neighbourhood m find hard cuts in a flattened clip? Run at CJ2a's head; it replaces VR-S2.
spikes.rule: Pick the signature (32-bin luma of 64×36, or 4×4×4 colour at long side 256) and T with the highest recall on flattened exports, with at most one false cut per 10 min on a no-cut talking head. m is the largest of 4/6/8/12 frames that loses no true cut on the fixture. It passes at recall ≥ 98 %. Otherwise add luma SAD as a second signal and repeat; if that fails, ship with the measured recall stated in the guide.
